items.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013
items.q: The kid plays like Bob Mintzer.

ctx.x: I think that’s a really interesting statement. Because it says you are trying to get your message out like a singer. Singers have the benefit and the burden of the words sometimes.

Yes. And their job is to relate that to the audience so that they can feel if there’s anger or if there’s pathos, whatever emotion that we’re trying to throw at them from the stage — joy or sorrow — that the audience can feel this at the same time. And I have this kid who’s a great tenor player, who’s at Fredonia. He’s a freshman — no he’s a sophomore now. He came as a freshman. The kid plays like Bob Mintzer. He just rips over it. Extensions, everything. But I’m trying to get his softer side in. So I found in…

have saxophone players who can double, which is fantastic. So I ran this out for him. He played such an aggressive solo, it was — I’d say this would be like on a date with your girlfriend in a car and you grab her by the shirt and you say, “I love you dammit.” I said, “she’d be out of the car in a heartbeat if you were doing that.” I said, “you’ve got to put some tenderness into it and realize what the lyrics are.” So I told him, “learn the lyrics. Play the lyrics, and tell the story that way.” And I also tell…
